newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-C&W Communications says may seek buys.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-C&W Communications says may seek buys.

text.p: Cable and Wireless Communications, Britain's new cable telephone and television giant, said on Monday it might seek further acquisitions.

"Here we've formed the (UK's) largest cable company, so we've taken the first step in the consolidation of the industry -- and we'll look at other acquisitiosn as and when they will arrive," new chief executive Graham Wallace told a journalist telephone conference call.
But he added: "We have a scale and mass here that gives us a significant advantage. We certaintly don't need to be any larger."

The merger, announced last October, brings together Cable and Wireless's Mercury subsidiary and the UK cable television units of NYNEX Corp, Nynex CableComms, Bell Canada's Bell CableMedia and Videotron.
The formal offers from Cable and Wireless Communications to shareholders of the merger partners were launched on Monday, slightly ahead of schedule, despite the enormous complexity of the deal.

Since last October, speculation has swept the market that first the merger had run into teething problems and then that a global telecoms alliance such as the Global One partnership of Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and America's Sprint Corp might take a stake in the venture.

With 14.7 percent of Cable and Wireless Communications (CWC) due to be floated in London and New York within the next few weeks, there will be an opportunity for new shareholders to join the group -- or old partners to leave.
Newspapers have tipped Bell Canada as being a likely candidate to sell what will be a 14.2 percent stake and end its exposure to the UK cable market.
But Wallace declined to comment on Bell Canada's long-term strategic plans, saying only: "It is very happy with the investment that it has in CW&C as far as we are aware."
France Telecom confirmed last week that it was in talks with Cable and Wireless about the cable venture becoming the British partner of the Global One alliance.
Wallace declined to comment on alliance speculation.

But he said Cable and Wireless, which will have a 52.6 percent stake in the company, wanted to remain a majority shareholder and would consider further investment of its own if its current partners backed out.
"C&W wish to remain with at least 50 percent of Cable and Wireless Communications and in the event of further investment being available to them, they would be interested looking at it," he said.

Analysts are keenly awaiting the partial float of Cable and Wireless Communications so that the market can value the business. With assets of 4.5 billion pounds, they have hung a price tag of between 4.5 and 7 billion stg on the company.
Britain will be the new company's short-term focus, Wallace said, although the group is eyeing continental Europe as well.

"We're in good shape to move the business forward," he said, adding that the huge amount of detailed information made public on Monday demonstrated what a unique company this would be in terms of its range, product and services both in telecoms and information.
"On top of the infrastructure that exists in these companies and the growing markets were in, were pretty optimistic about the future," he added.
The first closing date for the offers is April 25. A flotation will immediately follow a completion of the merger.
